doc.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

title: Playing the alphabet of songs to Atlantic City
summary: Sol tells of winning a bet by playing songs A to Z on the drive.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I once won a bet, Monk Rowe, in a car going to Atlantic City maybe fifteen years ago, that I couldn’t play the clarinet from New York to Atlantic City nonstop. I won a bet that time, a hundred dollar bet. And I played from New York to Atlantic City. I played songs starting off with the letter A, which was “All of Me” I remember as if it was yesterday, and the last song was Z, “Zing Goes the Strings of My Heart.” I must have played easy 183 songs. Maybe more, who the hell knows. Just one chorus. I would play like this [Sol plays]. Then I would think of another song with A, “All the Things You Are” [Sol plays]. Then I’d think of another song, A, “Alexander’s Ragtime Band” [Sol plays].
“Autumn in New York.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-
